The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts, and now the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers are coming to town, bringing one of the league's most complete rosters and a defense that has consistently given Dallas problems in their recent matchups.

There are some opportunities for the Cowboys, particularly with CeeDee Lamb playing at a high level, but there are also some difficult matchups that could expose weaknesses on Dallas' roster. Here are two players to buy and two to sell ahead of Sunday's game.

I mean, who else would this list start with? Lamb has been the best player for the Cowboys all season, and there's no reason to think that Dallas will stop feeding him the ball. Lamb is coming off a monster performance against Indianapolis, hauling in 10 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets. It was his second-highest receiving total in a game during his career.

Through nine games, Lamb has 70 receptions for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. He's already surpassed the 900-yard mark, and his 108 targets lead the Cowboys by a wide margin. The matchup against San Francisco is difficult, but Lamb is the kind of receiver who can change a game regardless of the opponent. With George Pickens possibly missing another week and Dallas dealing with inconsistencies elsewhere the offense, Dak Prescott should continue looking Lamb's way early and often.

The 49ers will undoubtedly have a plan for him, but Lamb's recent production makes him difficult to leave out of the buyers market. He's been the Cowboys' most reliable playmaker overall, and Dallas needs to find ways to get him involved.

At some point, the Cowboys have to figure out how to beat San Francisco, and Dak Prescott has to be a big part of that solution. Unfortunately, his history against the 49ers doesn't inspire much confidence. Prescott is 2-4 against San Francisco in his career, including an 0-2 record in the playoffs. In those two postseason games, he has thrown for 460 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. His most recent regular-season meetings haven't been much better. He threw three interceptions in the 2023 blowout loss and two more in the 2024 matchup.

Across his four regular-season games against San Francisco, Prescott has completed 65.5% of his passes for 875 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions. That's not necessarily disastrous production, but the turnovers have been costly, particularly against a team that knows how to capitalize on mistakes.

The 49ers have won four straight meetings against Dallas, and Prescott will have to overcome both that team history and his own struggles against this opponent. San Francisco's defense is disciplined, physical and capable of making quarterbacks pay for forcing throws.

With Fred Warner leading the unit, Prescott will have to be sharp with his reads and decision-making, especially against the blitz, where he has looked terrible this year. Dallas needs a big performance from its quarterback to pull off the upset. Given the history, though, this is a matchup where I'm selling Prescott until he proves otherwise.

With Jake Ferguson ruled out due to a knee injury, Brevyn Spann-Ford has an opportunity to take on an even bigger role in the Cowboys' offense. It might not be the most obvious matchup to exploit, but he could be a sneaky contributor against San Francisco.

Spann-Ford has caught 15 passes for 130 yards this season, and his role has been growing. Against Indianapolis, he played 55 offensive snaps compared to Ferguson's 27, catching two of three targets for 20 yards. That workload suggests the Cowboys are already comfortable giving him significant playing time.

The 49ers have plenty of defensive talent to account for, and their attention will naturally gravitate toward Lamb and the Cowboys' other primary playmakers. That could leave opportunities for Spann-Ford underneath or in the middle of the field, particularly if Dallas uses him to help with protection before releasing him into a route.

This isn't a prediction that Spann-Ford is suddenly going to become the focal point of the passing game. Rather, it's a bet that his increased playing time and the attention paid to Dallas' other weapons could create a few favorable opportunities. With Ferguson unavailable, the Cowboys need someone else to contribute from the tight end position. Spann-Ford is in a good position to do that.

The Cowboys have indicated that Jaishawn Barham could see an increased workload as injuries continue to pile up on the defensive side of the ball. That's understandable from a personnel standpoint, but it also creates a potential problem against an offense as versatile as San Francisco's.

Barham had some encouraging moments early in the season, but his limitations have become more apparent as the competition has increased. His playing time has also been limited recently, which makes the prospect of a larger role against the 49ers particularly concerning.

San Francisco is exactly the type of opponent that can put a young linebacker in difficult situations. Kyle Shanahan's offense uses motion, misdirection and mismatches to create space, and open up running lanes.

If Dallas gives him more responsibility, San Francisco will have plenty of opportunities to test him. The Cowboys need all the help they can get defensively, but this is a tough week to ask an inconsistent young player to take on a bigger role.

Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres has staked a strong claim for a regular starting berth under Mikel Arteta by netting in an eighth consecutive Nations League fixture. The 28-year-old scored a first-half brace on Saturday night to fire Sweden to a 3-2 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in Stockholm.

Gyokeres converted twice from the penalty spot as Potter's hosts surged into a three-goal half-time lead following Daniel Svensson's opener. The centre-forward also had an assist for Alexander Isak chalked off for offside before the visitors pulled two goals back. Saturday's triumph on November 14 secured Sweden's promotion back to League A for the first time since the 2020-21 campaign.

Finding the net for an eighth straight match in the competition means the marksman has now plundered 12 goals across that prolific sequence dating back to October 2024. Furthermore, he has only failed to score once across his last 11 outings in the tournament, with that solitary blank coming during a 2-2 draw against Slovakia two years ago.

His latest double lifts him onto 16 career goals in the tournament, placing him second on the all-time scoring chart behind only Norway striker Erling Haaland on 23 strikes. On the international stage, the forward has now registered 27 goals in 42 caps since making his senior bow aged 20 back in 2019.

That haul moves him into joint-ninth on his country's all-time scoring list alongside Agne Simonsson, having reached the mark in nine fewer appearances. He still trails Zlatan Ibrahimovic's national record of 62 goals by 35 strikes, although the former icon earned 80 more caps before retiring in 2023.

Saturday's milestone unfolded in front of 51,049 spectators at the Strawberry Arena, formerly known as the Friends Arena, setting a new attendance record for a men's national team match at the venue. That turnout surpassed the previous stadium benchmark of 49,967 set against England during its inaugural fixture in 2012, though Sweden's all-time home record remains the 52,943 crowd against West Germany at Rasunda Stadium on September 26, 1965.

Gyokeres will look to extend his streak when Sweden conclude their international window away against Poland on Tuesday. Returning to north London, the ex-Sporting CP striker hopes to kickstart a domestic campaign that has yielded just two goals in 14 outings across all competitions. #2633. Is everyone on Nets roster available for trade? Mostly yes

Is "everyone" on the Brooklyn Nets roster available for the right price as Sam Amick reported Friday in a round-up of trade rumors?!? Even 20-year-old Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin, the organization's two highest draft picks over the past 30 years?!? Seems a bit much, but with the Nets record disappointing as they get ready to play the Memphis Grizzlies at the end of a four-game road trip, the general sentiment appears true, as the The Athletic reporter noted.

If you call the Brooklyn Nets (3-8) about any of their players, they will listen. Per a team source, it's just that simple.

Such is life when you're a rebuilding team, not to mention an organization that has two veterans — Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle — who could help any number of contenders.

Those two players are widely discussed as top targets in league circles, with Porter (21.5 points and 7.5 rebounds per) above all the rest of the Nets. The 28-year-old small forward who won a title with Denver in 2023 is in the last year of his deal ($40.8 million). Randle, the 31-year-old forward who helped Minnesota reach the West finals in 2025, has a player option worth $35 million for next season.

Two days ago, Jake Fischer of The Steinline offered a similar assessment.

An expectation persists in some corners of the league that Brooklyn, which owes its first-rounder in June to Houston as a lingering vestige of the acquisition of James Harden in January 2021, might indeed decide to shop veterans such as Michael Porter Jr. via trade between now and Feb. 11 to see if it can capitalize on the anticipated lack of true sellers in the marketplace.

So, it's increasingly a given in NBA circles that the Nets will be a bazaar come February 12 at 3:00 p.m. EST or maybe even before, say December 15, the unofficial start of trade season when the dozens of players signed or re-signed over the Summer become available for the first time. The larger the pool of players, the more possibilities that GMs and capologists can noodle. Of course with all the injuries across the league, it's possible teams will want to find replacements earlier than that.

MPJ is the MMP of the group == Most Mentioned Player — for a number of reasons. He is having yet another good season as Amick notes and is on an expiring deal. If the Nets don't want to extend him — they can up till June 30 — then they'd better do something or lose him without a return. That is not going to happen. Randle is in a bit of a similar situation but he isn't expiring. He's got a player option and while he will be four years older than Porter Jr. by the deadline, his contract load is lighter. MPJ is owed $40.6 million this season, compared to the $33.3 million Randle makes now and the $35.8 million he'll earn if he doesn't exercise his option. He is expected to.

Otherwise, what's the Nets rush? That's where it gets interesting. For one thing, the Draft and off-season are when Sean Marks & co. makes their biggest moves and it's also when teams examine their futures a lot more closely. They know what the need. It wouldn't be surprising if the Nets look to add more assets for a big trade, even if they already had 13 first rounders and 19 seconds available. Do they have their eye on someone? Almost certainly, they have a list, but as Marks admitted on Brooklyn's Media Day in September, there's a lot that has to be considered, starting with who other teams are willing to part with.

Marks was specifically asked at Media Day when he might "push all the chips to the middle of the table" and make the big move for that player, as he has said, who will "absolutely and automatically change the trajectory of the franchise." He was generally non-committal, but did identify the factors that will come into play.

"We've got a couple more rookies this year to add into the fray as well," Marks said, suggesting he wants to see how his young players do this season. "But then it's also a combination of what becomes available, right? I can't predict when players from other teams become available, what free agency looks like down the road and so forth. So, I think that's where you just keep your flexibility and you know, like, okay, when's the right time to go for this?

"We're always listening. I'm not sure we're going to be any more active than we have been in the past, but that doesn't mean we're not listening. That doesn't mean we're not shaking trees and seeing what's out there. I think a lot will be predicated first and foremost on what this roster looks like, and we'll get a good feel for that pretty early." (Emphasis added.)

Of course, the Nets has been very very active in the recent past with the two franchise-defining trades with the Knicks and Rockets just before the the Draft in 2024, or the multiple salary dump deals just before the Draft in 2025 that got them MPJ and the Nuggets 2032 pick and the Hawks No. 22 pick. or just before the Draft in 2026 that got them Randle in the T'Wolves first round pick.

Bottom line, we think, is that the Nets are holding their cards close, maybe even closer than usual (which is saying something.) It makes sense, of course, because you can't keep accumulating assets forever. You have to move.

#2631. Independent experts to review handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation as NFL gives insight into process

How the investigation into the circumstances around Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clots will proceed is coming into focus.

Independent experts will look at the matter and share their findings with the NFL and NFLPA. The Eagles' Super Bowl MVP quarterback is expected to sit out the remainder of the 2026 season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.

In response to an October letter from Delaware Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, the NFL provided additional information to her office about the review, which has not officially begun.

"As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," Jeff Miller, NFL executive vice president of communications, public affairs and policy, said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester's office Friday.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) takes the snap against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Hurts was first said to have a superficial blood clot before the Eagles faced the Jaguars in London in Week 5, but still played in the game. He flew home with the team and practiced fully the following Wednesday.

A follow-up test showed the clot had moved, leading to the 28-year-old being placed on injured reserve on Oct. 17 with a diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) takes the snap from center Jake Majors (75) against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, in Tottenham. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The union called for a full investigation into the matter on Oct. 20, but it has not asked for a formal investigation into the health, safety or medical care provided by club-affiliated personnel, which it can under the CBA.

"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the NFLPA said in the statement last month. "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."

The neutral physicians selected must issue a written report within 60 days of being appointed. Both parties must act on those recommendations to address and correct any issues.

#2630. Kayla Harrison submits Amanda Nunes, lays claim to GOAT status at UFC 334

Kayla Harrison looked like she was ready to call it a night. She looked exhausted.

Then out of absolutely nowhere, the fight was over.

Harrison caught a Nunes kick, threw her a little off balance, ran to take her back, sank in a rear-naked choke – and forced the former two-division champion and consensus women's MMA GOAT to tap. Kayla Harrison (20-1 MMA, 4-0 UFC) retained the women's bantamweight title against Nunes (23-6 MMA, 16-3 UFC), who returned from a 3.5-year retirement to challenge for the belt.

Harrison's finish came at the 1:29 mark of the fourth round. The fight was her first attempted title defense and came after a layoff of nearly 18 months thanks to neck surgery and recovery.

Nunes caught the champ a couple times 100 seconds into the fight, then again seconds later. When Harrison clinched up, Nunes defended and drilled her a couple more times. Just short of two minutes in, Harrison again tried to tie her up and paid the price.

When they separated, Nunes backed her up quickly and continued to throw big punches with confidence. Harrison threatened with a takedown halfway through the round, but Nunes defended and got back to the middle and again came forward with hard pressure.

Harrison clipped Nunes with a left hand, then threw her to the canvas after Nunes tried to move around to her back. Nunes expertly reversed it and rolled out, but Harrison quickly re ersed again and tied up Nunes' right arm and landed short punches to the head. Harrison kept a headlock, then worked for an Americana. Nunes survived to see the second round, but it was a massive change of momentum.

In the second, Nunes initiated the wrestling with Harrison and found herself tied up. The former champ landed a few knees in the position, but ultimately got a takedown midway through the second – the first time Harrison had been taken down in the UFC. But with two minutes left, Harrison did the same as the first and landed a takedown that had her on top in side control working short ground-and-pound and looking for choke opportunities.

In the third, Harrison initiated a clinch, but Nunes didn't labor over a takedown attempt – heeding the warnings from her corner. But not long after that, Nunes caught Harrison off balance and used it for a takedown along the fence. Harrison looked tired, and had a blatant fence grab that helped her out that wasn't penalized. The fight went back to the feet midway through, but Nunes wound up on top when the fight spilled back down. She took Harrison's back and worked for a rear-naked choke, but was too high and Harrison worked her way to the top. With a minute left in the round, Harrison reeled back and landed a right elbow that cut Nunes open, and she landed another big punch with 15 seconds left and finished the round on top.

But in the fourth everything turned, and Nunes tapped for just the second time in her career.

#2627. Bayern star leaves France camp following Italy defeat

Bayern Munich centre-back Dayot Upamecano has departed the French national team camp.

The French Football Federation confirmed on Friday that the 28-year-old has left the camp early for personal reasons.

Upamecano played the full game as France suffered a 3-1 defeat to Italy in the UEFA Nations League on Thursday, despite taking an early lead through Michael Olise.

The Bayern defender conceded the penalty that allowed Pio Esposito to put Italy 3-1 ahead in the 74th minute.

France coach Zinedine Zidane has initially decided against calling up a replacement for Upamecano.

#2626. 3 Eagles tidbits coming out of the NFL trade deadline

NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared an NFL trade deadline notebook on ESPN that featured several mentions of the Philadelphia Eagles. Let's take a look at those here.

While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted — Dallas Goedert. Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027.

Not exactly shocking to see that teams had interest in acquiring him. Goedert is a solid tight end who could make nice contributions to a contending team.

At the same time, the Eagles didn't need to give him away for meager compensation. Especially when accounting for his salary cap ramifications.

It's interesting to see mention of the Eagles potentially keeping Goedert beyond 2026. It felt like the Eagles were close to moving on from him after each of the past two seasons. And he turns 32 in January. Are the two sides really going to do another one-year bandaid contract?

Maybe. The only Eagles tight end currently under contract beyond this season is … Eli Stowers. It wouldn't be very wise for the team to put all of their eggs in the basket of him panning out since the 2026 second-round pick has yet to show promise thus far.

The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles.

Interested to know exactly what the Bills were offering for Davis.

Nevertheless, seems like there was a bidding war for the Eagles' interior defender, which helps to explain why Howie Roseman was able to get such a big return from the jags.

The Eagles were not pleased that the Bengals reneged on their deal for Ebiketie after learning they would lose a third-round compensatory pick […]

Understandably so. The Eagles thought they had a done deal with the Bengals to ship out Ebiketie for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Before it became official, however, Cincy realized (thanks to compensatory picks expert Nick Korte) that acquiring Ebiketie would cause him to forfeit the 2027 third-round pick comp pick they were set to earn for losing Trey Hendrickson.

While one can understand why the Bengals wanted to back out after realizing their mistake, this failed trade is a pretty bad look for them.

I feel like the Bengals owe the Eagles one. Not exactly sure what that looks like but it's in Cincy's own interests to maintain healthy working relationships with other NFL general managers.
